name: LC Fine Foods
old_description: LC Cash and Carry, also known as LC Fine Food, is an establishment steeped in history, founded by the late and great Italo “Leo” Ciocca in the year 1965. Leo’s vision was to offer the finest Italian imports to his esteemed clientele. With his unwavering commitment to excellence and his unbridled passion for the food industry, Leo expanded his business, reaching new heights of success, while simultaneously adding new products and acquiring new customers across the wholesale and retail sectors. Today, his legacy lives on through LC Cash and Carry, where the tradition of offering authentic Italian products still remains strong, while at the same time, embracing the evolution of the market by adding a vast assortment of domestic products to cater to a wider audience.
about:
LC Fine Foods, operating as LC Cash and Carry, has been a fixture in New Haven, Connecticut since 1965. The company was founded by Italian immigrant Italo “Leo” Ciocca, who envisioned bringing the finest Italian imports to his community. What began as a modest enterprise grew steadily through Leo’s commitment to quality and service, establishing a reputation in the wholesale food trade.

Today the business functions as both a wholesale distributor and a cash-and-carry retailer, stocking a wide range of Italian and domestic food products. Its offerings span fresh produce, deli items, groceries, pasta, oils, cheeses, bakery goods, coffee, and seasonal specialties. The remodeled New Haven store serves walk-in customers six days a week, while a delivery operation supplies restaurants, delis, and institutions across the region.

The customer base includes independent restaurants, delicatessens, institutional kitchens, and retail shoppers. A deli owner in New Haven County describes the company as a primary supplier for fresh produce and cold cuts, while home cooks rely on it for traditional ingredients like San Marzano tomatoes and panettone. The firm also works with domestic and international suppliers, emphasizing relationships with local farmers and dairy producers.

The Ciocca family’s second generation, Carlo and Danny, now lead the company after Leo’s passing in 2023. They cite their differentiators as a family-owned legacy, direct supplier relationships, a commitment to local sourcing, and a service model that blends wholesale efficiency with retail accessibility.
